forecasts.note: Held. The adoption-saturation model is untouched by this week's flow, though a global term-premium repricing is exactly the macro regime it has never been tested in. Wide bars

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (NEW — the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Opens at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — 75% → 82%
hypotheses.d: Week's biggest mover, on three strands independent of the Israeli/exile channel. Pezeshkian said on Iranian state TV that communication with Khamenei is 'very difficult' — Tehran's own president, against his own interest. Washington routed its peace offer not to Araghchi but to Mohsen Rezaee, career IRGC commander-in-chief now running the security council. Cipher Brief: 'Tehran isn't saying who is actually in charge.' Capped at 82% because the state has promised footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders — that is the falsifier, and it is coming.

hypotheses.name: Nobody’s hurrying on Hormuz — HELD at 60%
hypotheses.d: The near-breakthrough-then-condition pattern fired a sixth time (Iran–Oman interim corridor and 30–60 days of technical talks, against Ghalibaf restating the full condition stack). Deliberately not moved: it is already priced, and a minesweeping calendar is what an honest process looks like too. The real test is live — the offer sits with the IRGC, so Tehran's answer is the experiment.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — 55% → 60%
hypotheses.d: The discriminating split signal arrived: PLA sorties kept declining while the coast guard escalated in kind — CCG 2307 pressing a Japanese coast guard ship in the strait Aug 6–10, which AEI reads as testing whether foreign vessels will obey PRC authority. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up is the ratchet signature. Capped at +5; the stated tell is what the coast guard does through the Sept 24 visit.

hypotheses.name: NEW · Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it opens at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts, and the reporting frames it in plain words as an alternative to Gulf oil routed through Hormuz. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Operation Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Mundane alternative, named and live: drugs, migration politics, regime-change, with the barrel a bonus. Falsifiers — cut hard if export volumes stay token (the $2-2.8bn tranches are a rounding error against control of 65bn bbl), if Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing does not actually swing off the Middle East, or if the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appears. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz, geography does not work that way — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Real Orinoco or Maracaibo channel-dredging and dedicated heavy-crude terminals WOULD be the premeditation tell. Unconfirmed today; it is the thing to watch.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — 45% → 52%
hypotheses.d: Economic Outcast hit ~60 teapots, tankers and traders and touched no Chinese state major and no bank — Treasury sent the majors a warning letter instead. Maximum pressure on Iran, calibrated to stop exactly short of anything that would detonate the Sept 24 summit. Held to +7 because the Munir offer is a real concession, and $4.10 gas before midterms is real evidence against premeditation.

hypotheses.name: NEW · A pre-announcement leak into oil futures
hypotheses.d: Four times in the war window, nine- and ten-figure short bets landed 15–20 minutes before an Iran announcement: ~$2.2bn across crude, gasoil and gasoline before Trump's Mar 23 pause post; ~$950m before the Apr 7 ceasefire; ~$760m before Iran said Hormuz would open. ~$7bn total; CFTC probing, four members of Congress demanding answers. Split: deliberate leak 45 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 25 / coincidence 10. This is the only entry in the book whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event rather than pattern-matched after — which is why it opens this high. Against it: no episode has surfaced around this week's diplomacy.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 30% → 25%
hypotheses.d: Cut again. The channels that actually moved this week were Oman, Pakistan and the new Mecca defence pact — Russia was absent from every one of them, and still has not offered the mediation this hypothesis expects. Motive 9/10, documentary evidence 0/10, pre-event evidence never. Cut to 15% if nothing surfaces by Sept 30.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Both its live predictions came in favourably this week and it gets credit for neither: the rival leverage hypothesis predicted the same things, and shared predictions are ambience. One more failed pre-summit call and it goes to the epitaph list.

brief.h: Two supertankers were struck by projectiles inside the southern Hormuz corridor Washington publicly declared cleared four days ago - one of them Saudi state tonnage
brief.t: The story is not the two hulls, it is the warranty. On 28 August Admiral Brad Cooper announced that US forces had cleared Iran's mines from the internationally recognised lanes, citing nearly 1,500 vessels escorted through. Overnight the Saudi-flagged Sidr, run by the kingdom's state carrier Bahri, was hit northeast of Khasab, and Sinokor's Senegal Prosperity took three projectiles east of Oman - both inside that lane, with Iran separately claiming a sea-mine strike on a tanker. Follow the money and the machine appears: a great power issued a safety guarantee over a waterway, and the people who actually price that guarantee are not admirals but underwriters, who now have two data points against a four-day-old claim.
brief.context: Name the desk: the body that decides whether Hormuz is open is the Joint War Committee at Lloyd's, which sets the listed-areas breach premium every shipowner pays, not CENTCOM's press room. That is why our Hormuz reopening number keeps falling while the diplomacy keeps sounding better - reopening is an actuarial event, not a political one, and actuaries price incident frequency in a specific lane over a specific quiet period. The base rate is the Tanker War of 1984-88, when 451 merchant ships were attacked in these waters and traffic recovered only after a ceasefire plus a full convoy regime, never during an active attack series. The deeper rail is older still: since 1988 the United States has underwritten Gulf shipping in exchange for a dollar-invoiced oil trade, and a warranty voided in 96 hours is a small precise crack in that bargain rather than its end. Influence map: principals Washington and Riyadh, agent CENTCOM, narrator the clearance statement, operator the war-risk underwriter, market a Brent curve above 92 dollars, target the shipowner who pays more either way. Falsifier for our read - if no laden tanker is attacked inside the international lanes through 22 September and Muscat publishes a minesweeping calendar, we score the recurrence call a miss rather than deferring it, and mark reopening back up.

angles.effect: Buys the destruction of a claim rather than of a ship. Neither hull sank; what was destroyed was the credibility of a public American clearance statement, which is far cheaper to attack than a warship.
Pays in the currency it chose. Announcing a clearance converted every later incident in that lane from an Iranian provocation into an American failure - a liability transfer nobody forced on it.

Learns its own state tonnage is inside the target set. Bahri is not a flag of convenience, it is the kingdom's shipping arm, and this is the first datum that pushes Saudi hedging rather than Saudi patience.
Collect and pay respectively. Breach premiums are charged per voyage on a listed area, so every incident is revenue for the syndicate and cost for the charterer, whether or not anything is hit.
Gain quietly. Every month the strait stays expensive is a month the East-West line and Fujairah earn a scarcity premium they cannot earn when Hormuz is normal.

dec.kill: A struck US-flagged hull or a confirmed American death would break the intercepted-volley equilibrium and turn this from an insurance story into a campaign. Conversely a Joint War Committee decision NOT to re-rate the southern corridor, plus three weeks with no attack on a laden tanker, would mean the clearance claim substantially held and these two strikes were the tail of the Aug 30 exchange rather than the start of a series.

brief.h: Japan's 10-year yield touched 3 percent for the first time since 1996 and Britain's 10-year gilt hit 5.25 percent, its highest since 2008 - the war's bill arrived at the sovereign bond desk
brief.t: This is the most important thing on the board today and almost nobody will lead with it. Yields blew out together across five countries - Japan's 10-year at 3 percent with its 5-year at a record 2.26, the gilt at a 2008 high, the Bund at a 2011 high, the French OAT at a 2008 high, the US 30-year at 5.27 - and the drivers the market names are one shock and one habit: Brent above 92 dollars with European gas at its highest since March, and deficits nobody is consolidating. Follow the money and the mechanism is a rollover. Governments termed out enormous borrowing in 2020 and 2021 at roughly 1 percent; that paper now matures into a market charging four to five, and the difference is not a forecast, it is an invoice already written.
brief.context: R0, date the rail: this is a late chapter of the Bank of Japan epoch - zero rates in 1999, quantitative easing in 2001, yield-curve control in 2016 - which made the yen the world's cheapest funding currency for a generation. Everything from Australian mortgages to American Treasury demand has been quietly subsidised by Japanese institutions reaching abroad for yield they could not get at home; at 3 percent they no longer need to, and the money comes home. The desk that decides is not a central-bank podium but the Japanese life insurers and the primary dealers who have to clear each auction, which is why an auction tail matters more than a governor's speech. Framework: Kennedy's imperial overstretch as sharpened by Ferguson - US net interest outlays now exceed defence spending - carried with the honest caveat that Kennedy's framework famously mis-called Japan in the 1980s and Nye has been right that declinism cries wolf. Base rate: term-premium regime shifts are rare and sticky, roughly one a generation, which argues against reading one morning as the turn. Falsifier: long yields in three G7 countries falling 50 basis points before December with the Middle East file still open would mark this an inflation scare, not a structural repricing.

angles.effect: Pay first and pay most. That vintage was issued near 1 percent and refinances at four to five, which crowds out discretionary spending without a single vote being taken.
Gains the veto. A higher term premium is the market repricing the risk of being repaid in debased money - the one constituency that can discipline a treasury without an election.
Gain genuinely, for the first time in thirty years. Domestic yield ends the forced march abroad - which is precisely why the rest of the world loses a buyer.
Pay the transmission. When the risk-free curve rises everywhere, frontier issuers reprice by more - the thread that connects this card to Zambia's.

angles.party: Anyone financing three theatres at once
angles.effect: Faces triage. Hormuz convoys, Ukraine resupply and a Pacific buildup cost the same in hulls and very different amounts in interest.

dec.kill: A tailed or failed JGB or gilt auction would confirm this is a funding event rather than a price move. A clean run of auctions with long yields drifting back down as oil retreats would mean the market was pricing the strait, not the sovereign.

brief.h: Xi, Putin, Modi, Pezeshkian and Erdogan signed 28 documents in Bishkek including a ports and logistics action plan through 2030 - and left Ukraine out of the declaration entirely
brief.t: Discard the photograph and read the annex. The headline item is Putin proposing an SCO Development Bank and citing 400 billion dollars of Russia-SCO trade; the load-bearing item is a signed 2026-2030 action plan for member states' ports and logistics centres, agreed in the same month a chokepoint is running at a tenth of normal. A bank proposed at intervals since 2010 and never capitalised is a speech; a multi-year logistics programme with a date range is a rail. What is absent matters as much: the declaration omits the Ukraine war altogether and manages only deep concern about the Middle East - a bloc that will not name either of the two wars its own members are fighting or blockaded by.
brief.context: Brzezinski warned in The Grand Chessboard that the one combination Washington could not manage was a China-Russia-Iran antihegemonic coalition, and that it would be built on grievance rather than shared interest - which is exactly why it produces communiques faster than instruments. The desk that decides here is not the leaders' hall but the transport ministries and the Chinese policy banks that would have to fund a corridor, and their revealed preference has been bilateral Belt and Road lending rather than a pooled facility, because pooling means sharing control with India. Source discipline first: the document list comes from TASS, Russian state media covering a summit Russia co-chairs, so the omissions are more trustworthy than the claims. Base rate on the bank: sixteen years of proposals, zero capital. The layer that matters is the operator - whoever actually dredges a berth and signs an offtake - because that is where a bypass either exists or does not. Falsifier for the sceptical read: a named, capitalised SCO facility with a headquarters and a first disbursement before mid-2027 would mean the instrument arrived and we were wrong.

angles.effect: Gains the room. Being photographed as a co-equal convener four years into sanctions is the cheapest thing Russia bought this year, and it cost one speech.

Gains a stage and concedes nothing. China funds corridors bilaterally where it sets the terms, and a pooled bank carrying Indian votes is a downgrade - which is why sixteen years of proposals have gone nowhere.
Buys optionality and pays in Western trust. Modi stands in the photo, urges Putin to end the war, and declines the bank. The classic hedge, and it is not free.

Gets the appearance of a bloc without a defence clause. Pezeshkian arrived offering to reciprocate immediately if Washington returns to the June MOU, which tells you where he thinks the file actually gets settled.
Pays nothing here, and that is the finding. A summit of ten states that will not name the largest war in Europe is not a mediation venue.

dec.kill: A capitalised SCO Development Bank with a first disbursement, or a mutual-defence clause appearing in a later declaration, would convert choreography into architecture. Another anniversary summit in 2027 with a longer document count and no funded instrument confirms the read.

brief.h: Russia struck Odesa's port export facilities, its energy grid and the border crossing into Romania overnight, and killed seven at a Kyiv railway depot - hours after Modi asked Putin in Bishkek to end the war
brief.t: Note what was hit. Not the line of contact, but the door goods leave through: Zelenskyy said the strike deliberately damaged a border crossing point with Romania as well as export infrastructure, while glide bombs and drones left thousands of households in the region without power. That is coercion aimed at Ukraine's revenue and at the patience of the European states on the far side of that crossing - and it landed on the same day Russia's president stood in Bishkek invoking the anniversary of the 1939 invasion of Poland to warn against letting confrontations escalate. The distance between those two sentences is the analysis.
brief.context: The mechanism is the export valve, and it is the oldest instrument in this war: grain, metals and now the road link to a NATO member are the assets Kyiv monetises and Moscow can reach without taking ground. Belligerents settle when their expectations about the future converge - Reiter's finding, and Freedman's theory-of-victory test - so striking the export door is a bid to move Ukraine's expectation, not evidence that Russia's has moved. The base rate is discouraging and we publish it as such: roughly 79 percent of interstate wars end within two years, and this one is in its fifth, deep in the tail where the odds of stopping fall rather than rise. The desk to watch is not the summit hall but the Russian targeting cycle, which has spent the summer alternating between grid and logistics, and the second-order loser is Romania, which absorbs the risk of ordnance landing metres from its territory without a vote. Our ceasefire forecast is unchanged at 15 percent, and today is the reason it did not move.

brief.h: Hakainde Hichilema was sworn in for a second term with the runner-up who took 38 percent of the vote in custody on treason charges, and the courts sealed on the last day a challenge could be filed
brief.t: Zambia is not a footnote, it is the test case. This is the country that became Africa's first pandemic-era sovereign default in November 2020 over a missed 42.5 million dollar coupon, then spent five years as the G20 Common Framework's showpiece - roughly 94 percent of the debt inside the restructuring perimeter now covered, an IMF programme concluded, copper output climbing, growth projected near 5.8 percent for 2026. Follow the money and the trade becomes visible: the restructuring bought Hichilema enormous external legitimacy, and external legitimacy substitutes for the domestic kind. Brian Mundubile went into hiding after a raid on his home on 14 August, surrendered, and was charged with treason; the courts were sealed on the final day an election petition could be filed. The creditors have said nothing, because nothing in the framework asks them to.
brief.context: Name the mechanism: creditor conditionality prices compliance, not consent. The Common Framework was built after 2020 to coordinate Paris Club and Chinese lending, and it carries fiscal and transparency conditions with no political clause whatsoever - so a government that services its restructured debt and hits its primary-balance target is a good sovereign borrower regardless of who is in a cell. The desk that decides is the Official Creditor Committee co-chairs plus China Exim, Zambia's largest single creditor, with roughly 3.3 billion dollars of commercial obligations still under active negotiation, which gives Lusaka a live interest in creditor goodwill and gives creditors an interest in a stable counterparty. Then layer on the metal: copper is the electrification input both Washington and Beijing are competing for - Washington through the Lobito corridor, Beijing through ownership - and neither spends leverage on a treason charge against a supplier it is courting. The base rate is blunt: African incumbents who jail the runner-up rarely face material creditor or Fund consequence. Name the incompetence alternative too - sealed courts on a filing deadline can be bureaucratic panic rather than design, and no one has yet produced an order. Falsifier: an Official Creditor Committee statement, a delayed IMF review, or a Lobito or Millennium Challenge disbursement paused on governance grounds before December would mean the political clause exists in practice even though it does not exist on paper.

angles.effect: Converts a creditor success into a domestic shield. A president who cleared 94 percent of a default is very hard for any external actor to lecture about process.
Pay the whole cost. A 38 percent vote share with no filed petition, because the building was closed, is the specific injury here.
Gain a compliant debtor and pay in the framework's credibility. A restructuring architecture indifferent to how the debtor governs will be read as indifferent everywhere it is next used.
Both gain and neither moves. Copper access is the shared interest, and governance objections are the first thing dropped when a supply chain is contested.

Carry the residual. Growth near 5.8 percent alongside a fiscal deficit running at 5 percent of GDP against a 2.1 percent target is a bill that lands as subsidy cuts - now with less recourse to contest it.

dec.kill: A named creditor or IMF action tied to the detention - a delayed review, a paused disbursement, a joint statement - would falsify the read that the framework is politically blind. Silence from every creditor through December, with the next review passing normally, confirms it.

lesson: Paul Kennedy called it imperial overstretch: a great power's commitments outrun the economic base that pays for them, and the reckoning arrives not on a battlefield but at a bond auction. Niall Ferguson sharpened it into a rule of thumb now known as Ferguson's Law - any empire that spends more servicing its debt than defending itself is in decline - and the United States crossed that line when net interest outlays passed the defence budget. Today's tape is what the mechanism looks like in real time. Britain's 10-year gilt at 5.25 percent, Germany's Bund at a 2011 high, France's OAT at a 2008 high, the US 30-year at 5.27 percent and Japan's 10-year at 3 percent for the first time since 1996 - all on the same morning, all driven by the same two inputs: an energy shock coming through a contested strait, and deficits nobody is consolidating. The Japanese number is the one to hold onto, because for thirty years near-zero yen funding was the shock absorber that let every other government borrow cheaply; when Tokyo pays 3 percent, Japanese institutions bring their money home and the absorber stops absorbing. What this predicts is not collapse but triage - a state financing Hormuz convoys, Ukraine resupply and a Pacific buildup at 5 percent instead of 1 percent has to drop something, and the honest guess is that it drops the least visible commitment first rather than the loudest. Keep the guardrail on, though: Kennedy's framework spent the 1980s forecasting Japanese ascendancy and American decline and got both backwards, and Joseph Nye has been right for forty years that declinism cries wolf. So here is the narrow, falsifiable version - if long yields in three of the G7 retreat by 50 basis points before December while the Middle East file stays open, this was an inflation scare rather than a structural repricing, and the overstretch reading should be marked down accordingly.

lecture.title: The Economic Weapon: Why Sieges Make the Wars They Mean to Prevent

sections.t: Treasury designated roughly sixty Chinese “teapot” refiners — the small plants buying discounted Iranian crude — while touching no Chinese state major and no bank. The same week, central banks bought a record 288.9 tonnes of gold in the quarter gold fell over 20%. Two stories, one machine.

sections.h: Follow the money, name the mechanism
sections.t: A reserve manager buying into a 20% drawdown is not trading. He is hedging ACCESS — the risk that an asset held abroad gets switched off by its host government — and gold is the only large reserve asset with no counterparty who can flip that switch. Name the mechanism: the ECONOMIC WEAPON, using the financial plumbing whose hubs one country owns to inflict a siege without laying one. Iran discounts crude to Chinese teapots paying through dollar-touching chains; Treasury designates them; the IRGC's Strait Authority recoups the shortfall in Hormuz tolls. Sanction and gold bar are one transaction seen from two ends.

sections.h: Deep history I — the blockade that became an idea
sections.t: The economic weapon has a birthday and a founding failure. The birthday is November 1806, when Napoleon's Berlin Decrees declared the British Isles blockaded — the Continental System, an attempt to beat a maritime power by closing a continent's markets to it. It succeeded at nothing except generating enforcement. Portugal would not comply, so France invaded in 1807 and got the Peninsular War, the ulcer that bled the Grande Armée for six years. Alexander I quit the system in December 1810 because it was ruining Russian trade, and in 1812 Napoleon marched east to enforce it. The blockade never defeated Britain; it manufactured the two wars that destroyed the blockader. Sanctions require enforcement, and enforcement against a determined leakage path tends toward conquest. The second case mattered because it worked. The Allied blockade of Germany ran from 1914 through the armistice and was lifted only when Germany signed at Versailles in June 1919. German official estimates put civilian deaths from malnutrition near 424,000 — contested, and historians still argue how much was blockade and how much German agricultural mismanagement. But perception makes policy, and a generation concluded hunger had beaten an undefeated army. So they institutionalized it as a PEACE instrument: Article 16 of the League Covenant made sanctions automatic against an aggressor, and Wilson in 1919 put it in words no Treasury official would dare use today — “A nation that is boycotted is a nation that is in sight of surrender. Apply this economic, peaceful, silent, deadly remedy and there will be no need for force.” The weapon was invented to ABOLISH war; the rest of the century refutes that sentence.

sections.h: Deep history II — the failures that define our problem
sections.t: ABYSSINIA, 1935. Italy invaded Ethiopia; the League invoked Article 16 — exempting oil, coal and steel, and never closing the Suez Canal, which Britain controlled and through which Italian troopships sailed. Mussolini won anyway. The sanctions were real enough to enrage and too porous to stop, and the lesson is sharper than “sanctions don't work”: a sanction calibrated to spare the sender teaches the target that the sender is deterred too. Then the second-order effect. Nicholas Mulder's argument in The Economic Weapon is that the interwar regime deterred small states and PROVOKED large ones. Italy, Germany and Japan drew the same conclusion from the 1930s — dependence on seaborne trade was a vulnerability an enemy could switch off at will, and the answer was autarky, self-sufficiency taken by force. Lebensraum and the Co-Prosperity Sphere were ideological projects; they were also sanctions-proofing programs. Japan is the proof case. Washington embargoed scrap iron in 1940, then froze Japanese assets on 26 July 1941; America supplied roughly 80% of Japan's oil, and with Britain and the Dutch East Indies following, Japan lost about 88% of its oil imports. Reserves would last three years at peace, half that at war — Nagano's image was of a patient wasting away, every month of compliance leaving Japan weaker against the enemy it expected to fight. Pearl Harbor came in December. And the detail that turns story into discipline: the freeze was never meant to be total. Roosevelt intended a licensing regime keeping oil flowing so the tap stayed usable as leverage; officials in State and Treasury administered it so strictly that no licences issued and the flow stopped. The sanction that helped produce Pearl Harbor was substantially an organizational outcome, not a presidential decision — Allison's Essence of Decision, live. Before inferring “Iran's strategy” from one action, ask which bureau took it.

sections.h: The pattern — and where it breaks
sections.t: The leakage path is always the whole story — not the designation list, the leak: Portugal and Russia in 1806, Beira and Pretoria in 1966, Chinese teapots now. NOW THE BREAK. Japan in 1941 had a military option that promised to SOLVE its resource problem: seize the Dutch East Indies and own the oil. Iran has none — it fought its war, lost the conventional exchange, and has played its asymmetric card, the Hormuz toll. Nor did 1914 face an alternative supplier: Iran's is the world's second-largest economy, which the sanctioner just spared. Less Pearl Harbor, more Rhodesia.

MULDER says the siege provokes: strangulation drives large states to autarky, then preemption. DREZNER says sanctions are cheap theater — Hufbauer's data give a third success rate at best, near zero against great powers. The 2026 evidence buries neither: it splits by SIDE, and the split is the finding. On the TARGET Mulder scores: gold, stockpiles, payment rails, enrichment acceleration under maximum pressure. On the SENDER Drezner scores harder — the carve-outs. Sixty teapots and not one bank is not escalation; it is the sanctioner taking its own threat hostage, because hitting a Chinese bank endangers the dollar system that makes the hammer heavy.

The 2015 architecture is not coming back (high confidence): the 2022 freeze of Russian reserves turned the settlement network into an instrument; a hedge once bought is not resold. Expect bifurcation, not de-dollarization (moderate-high). EICHENGREEN is right that currencies erode glacially; the WEAPON depreciates faster than the CURRENCY. The bolder call (moderate): the most dangerous decade is the one in which the weapon still works but no longer terrifies. Mulder's mechanism fires in the transition — invested in escaping, not finished, expecting strangulation regardless. For China, the 2030s — so Economic D-Day may SHORTEN the fuse it was meant to lengthen. FALSIFIER: designate a major Chinese state bank; if Beijing cuts Iranian purchases within a quarter, I am wrong. Two centuries say the economic weapon does not replace war — it sorts the world into blocs that survive each other's sieges, then gives the survivors a reason to fight.

Nicholas Mulder, The Economic Weapon (2022) — published weeks before the Russia sanctions matched its template. Farrell & Newman, “Weaponized Interdependence” (2019) — it called the 2022 playbook and the chip controls in advance. Eichengreen, Exorbitant Privilege — the counterweight.

fired: FIRED - Hormuz/Iran, and for the first time on the STRICTER wording adopted Aug 27. That wire reads: an attack on a US-flagged or US-escorted vessel, OR an attack Iran publicly claims. Both conditions were touched overnight - two very large crude carriers struck by projectiles inside the southern corridor US forces escort and publicly declared cleared on Aug 28 (Bahri's Saudi-flagged Sidr northeast of Khasab; Sinokor's Senegal Prosperity hit by three projectiles east of Oman, UKMTO logging the second), and Iran separately claiming a sea-mine strike on a tanker. This fire is worth more than the four before it precisely because the wire was narrowed first: the old version fired 121 times this year and was a counter, not a signal.

NOT fired, and this is the limit of the above: the hulls are Saudi and South Korean, not US-flagged. No confirmed American deaths, no struck US hull. The intercepted-volley equilibrium has not broken yet.

NOT fired, checked and logged so the non-fire is scoreable: no blocking designation on a top-ten Chinese bank; no Kremlin acceptance of any limited ceasefire; no ferry requisition, reserve mobilization or missile dispersal near Taiwan; no summit-cancellation signal, with Xi in Bishkek exactly as the calendar said; no verified IRGC or Basij defection; no strike on Kharg's loading terminals.

armed: A struck US-flagged hull or a confirmed American death - the falsifier on the whole intercepted-volley equilibrium, and now the only escalation trigger left unfired in the strait

A war-risk re-rating of the southern Hormuz corridor by the Joint War Committee, or a withdrawal of the US clearance claim - the actuarial event that governs GEO-001 far more than any diplomatic announcement
